hook.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
hook.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
hook.sanskrit: सोऽहं कितवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामुने / नैकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्य पराजयम्
hook.line: Caught between two people you love, you can't cheer for one without losing the other.
hook.translation: I am like the mother of two gamblers playing against each other, great sage. I cannot wish one victory without wishing the other defeat.
hook.why: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

prasang.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
prasang.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who guided a war, admitted to a sage that he could not keep the peace in his own family.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

hook.for_you: You keep going over two offers and feel you are losing the other, caught like a mother who cannot cheer for one son without wishing the other defeat.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
alternates.sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
alternates.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
alternates.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
alternates.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
alternates.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.for_you: You are caught between two futures, and choosing one feels like losing the other. This is the bind you are in right now. Both paths hold what you care about.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you feel the loss of the other option, and let it sit without deciding.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verse.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verse.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verse.why: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

prasang.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
prasang.story_hook: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
prasang.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

verse.for_you: You feel you are losing the other with every choice, but the mind only grows full when it is fed. The two offers can stay. You do not have to feed the worry.
verse.try_today: Notice when you are feeding the worry, and let the thought go for one minute.
verse.scene_line: You stand between two paths, and the mind keeps adding fuel to the fire of doubt.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
worry is shown to live on the attention it is fed

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On this path, no beginning is lost and no harm results. Even a small amount of this practice protects from great fear. The tradition reads this as a path of action where every step forward counts, and even a little effort shields one from the fear of birth and death.
verse.for_you: You are not losing either offer by leaning into one. Even a small step forward shields you from the fear of this decision.
verse.try_today: Notice the part of you that is afraid of choosing wrong.
verse.scene_line: You stand at a crossroads like Arjuna, yet even a small practice shields from great fear.

why: answers the worry that an unfinished effort is a wasted one
Even a little of this path protects from great fear.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.for_you: You are not losing the other offer every time you choose one. Each path carries smoke. Pick the work that suits you and stay with it.
verse.try_today: Notice one flaw in your chosen work and let it be there.

why: flaws in the work are no reason to drop it; every undertaking has them
keeps a resolve from breaking on the first flaw

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रात्रौ सुखं वसेत् / अष्टमासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धः सुखं वसेत् / यावज्जीवं तु तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत्
verse.line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.
verse.translation: Do during the day what lets you sleep in peace at night; do in the eight dry months what lets you live comfortably through the rains. Do in youth what makes old age comfortable, and do all your life what brings peace after death.
verse.why: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

verse.for_you: You are losing nothing by choosing. You are gaining a clear conscience. Let the choice stand until the sun sets.
verse.try_today: Notice which offer lets you rest before the day ends.
verse.scene_line: You stand between two futures, and the night is already asking you to choose.

why: Choose today's act by how it will sit at night
Each stretch of time prepares the next

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Having searched all of Lanka without finding Sita, Hanuman fights off despair.
verse.sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
verse.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
verse.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
verse.why: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

prasang.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
prasang.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
prasang.story_hook: Hanuman had searched every palace in Lanka by moonlight, and she was nowhere.
prasang.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

verse.for_you: You keep weighing the two offers against each other. The choice itself is not the trap. The trap is the fear that choosing one means losing the other. You can still search for a third path.
verse.try_today: Notice one small detail you have not yet considered about either offer.

why: a concrete plan: the places not yet searched
Lakshmana and Hanuman both set the will to go on against despair, inside scenes of real loss.

story.title: Hanuman's unease in Ravana's chambers
story.story_hook: Hanuman, sent to find a stolen queen, ends up in a room no decent person should enter, and stops to ask whether he has just lost himself.
story.summary: Searching Ravana's palace at night, Hanuman finds himself looking across Ravana's sleeping wives and is seized by fear that he has broken dharma. He examines his own mind, finds it unmoved, reasons that the search itself required it, and goes on searching with a clear conscience.
story.lesson: Judge yourself by your intention and your mind's state, not only by what your eyes happened to meet while doing your duty.
story.teaser: Hanuman, sent to find a stolen queen, ends up in a room no decent person should enter, and stops to ask whether he has just lost himself.
